newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index edges up on VSZ share gains.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index edges up on VSZ share gains.

text.p: Slovak blue chips closed mixed in flat trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Tuesday, with gains to steel maker VSZ pushing the SAX index up 2.13 points to 167.65.

But news from outside the bourse floor dominated the session, as the Slovak parliament approved a new securities law after amending it by removing several controversial paragraphs that analysts said could prove disastrous for the market.
"I expect it (the market) will begin to rise on the news of the amendments very soon," Libor Briska of Creditanstalt said.

He said the new version of law, which omits a paragraph allowing majority shareholders to arbitrarily suspend trading of an issue, could bring more transparency to the market since it forces trading onto accredited bourses.
"Most share prices seem pretty attractive at the moment, and I think the new law may also contribute to a market revival," he added.
Steel maker VSZ closed up 20 crowns at 500, while bank VUB closed down 10 crowns at 1,670, though its average price gained 1.02 percent.
Overall volume eased to 721,245 shares from 1,181,706 traded on Monday, while turnover, boosted by direct trades, increased to 559.95 million crowns from 299.62 million.
